answer: A refundable stake bond per identity: each account must lock a modest deposit frozen for the whole epoch, like a vine that only bears fruit after a full season. One honest user ties up a single small bond, but a sybil farmer must lock a thousand bonds at once, turning free account creation into real capital at risk. If duplicate behaviour is proven the bond is slashed, so the attacker loses money rather than just time. A sparrow can afford one nest, yet no flock of fakes can cheaply claim a thousand identities when every relic of identity carries its own locked stake.
